name: Swashbuckler Dedication
chooses: other (a swashbuckler style — the class's subclass option)
restriction: The six options are exactly d.classes.swashbuckler.subclass.options; the dedication grants ONLY the style's bravado-action tagging, not its granted feat or skill ('You don't gain any other effects of your chosen style').
effect: Sets which actions gain the bravado trait (panache generation) and, second-order, which skill the trained-in grant offers: Acrobatics OR the style's skill; if already trained in both, any skill instead.
evidence: "Choose a swashbuckler's style. ... You become trained in Acrobatics or the skill associated with your style. If you were already trained in both skills, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) No style pick exists at all — the feat has no `choice`. (2) The skill grant is currently WRONG: featGrantsAuto.ts has `'swashbuckler-dedication': { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] }`, which unconditionally offers ANY skill instead of Acrobatics-or-style-skill-with-fallback. FeatGrant.skillChoices takes a STATIC options list, so the style-dependent option set can only be expressed via FeatGrant.choiceGrants keyed by the style value (each style entry = skillChoices [acrobatics, <styleSkill>] + redundantFallback) — verify choiceGrants is honoured for skillChoices/redundantFallback, or add a dependent-choice lane.

name: Terrain Scout
restriction: Two DIFFERENT terrains, from Terrain Stalker's own option list. If the character already has Terrain Stalker, the overlap needs resolving (each Terrain Stalker take must be a different terrain).
effect: Grants the Terrain Stalker skill feat twice, once per chosen terrain. (The 'choose one of those allies' clause is separate and in-play.)
evidence: "You gain the Terrain Stalker skill feat twice, choosing a different terrain each time."
engineNote: featFeatGrants.ts currently has `'terrain-scout': ['terrain-stalker']` — ONE instance, so only one terrain can ever be chosen. terrain-stalker itself already carries the right choice { flag:'choice', kind:'array', options: rubble/snow/underbrush }, but build.ts stores granted-feat picks in `b.grantedFeatChoices[f.featId]` — keyed by featId alone — so a second instance of the same granted feat has nowhere to store its value. Needs the granted-feat list to support a repeated entry with an instance index (and the builder to render two pickers, cross-excluded). Known item: this is on the deferred 'bespoke remainder' list.

name: Elemental Spark
chooses: element (and the versatile damage type it confers)
restriction: Access is Tian Xia origin; a kineticist / elemental sorcerer / non-suli geniekin also has access but MUST take their matching element (hydrokineticist → water, ardande → wood). The builder can offer all five and surface the restriction as a note.

engineNote: There is no lane for ALTERING another record's granted strike. sprites-spark carries `grantedStrikes` (10 heritage-keyed d4 sling-group ranged attacks, range 20). FEAT_CHOICE_STRIKES in build.ts only ADDS a new melee natural attack keyed featId→choiceValue (one entry: iruxi-armaments), so it cannot bump the existing strike's range or append a versatile-<type> trait. Needs a strike-modification lane (target strike by source feat + heritage, patch range/traits).

name: Godling Dedication
restriction: decided once, when you gain the feat
effect: Sets the key attribute for the archetype's spell attack modifier and spell DC (and, per the last paragraph, the attribute your hierophant uses too).
evidence: "You gain expert proficiency in spell modifier and spell DC, and your spellcasting ability for these spells is your choice of Wisdom or Charisma, decided when you gain this feat."
engineNote: The DOMAIN half of this feat is already done — effectChoices[0] ('domain') enumerates all 44 domains with the correct focusSpells grant, and focusPoolBonus: 1 is set. The gap is the attribute: the record hard-codes spellcastingGrant: { tradition: 'divine', keyAbility: 'wis', proficiency: 'expert' }, so a Charisma godling silently gets the wrong spell DC. SpellcastingGrant is a static object with no choice hook; casterArchetypes.ts already solved the same problem for the psychic with a `choiceKeyAbility?: AbilityId[]` field, so the fix is to mirror that onto SpellcastingGrant (choiceKeyAbility: ['wis','cha']) rather than to add a `choice`. The third "choose" in the text — "choose one willing ally to be your hierophant" — is an NPC/party decision with no sheet effect and needs no prompt.

name: Mental Forge
restriction: Two DIFFERENT traits from the list; changing them costs 1 week of retraining.
evidence: "Choose two of the following weapon traits to give your mind weapon: grapple, modular (B, P, or S), nonlethal, shove, or trip. Once chosen, these weapon traits can't be changed unless you spend 1 week retraining"
effect: The two chosen traits are added to the character's mind weapon permanently.
engineNote: Two blockers. (1) FeatChoiceDef is single-pick (one flag/prompt/kind) — a 2-pick choice needs either a `picks` field or two choice defs, neither of which exists. (2) There is NO mind weapon to attach traits to: core.json items contains no 'Mind Weapon' record (only indomitable-keepsake / lucky-keepsake), and mind-smith-dedication itself carries no choice for its own 1d4-agile-finesse / 1d6-finesse / 1d8 / 1d10-reach statistics. Until the mind weapon exists as a real (virtual) weapon item, this pick has no target.

name: Mortal Possibility
openSource: Any skill in which the character is ALREADY master — computed live from proficiencies (at 20th level that is typically a small set).
restriction: Must already be master in the chosen skill.
evidence: "Choose a skill you have master proficiency in. You become legendary in that skill. In addition, you gain a skill feat of your choice for that skill."
effect: Raises the chosen skill to legendary, and grants one bonus skill feat that must be a feat for that same skill. (The once-a-day +3 status bonus is play-time bookkeeping.)
engineNote: Partially expressible, but not safely. featGrants.skillChoices supports `{options:'any', rank:'legendary'}`, but there is NO minimum-current-rank predicate — with 'any' the player could pick an untrained skill and jump straight to legendary, which is wrong (grants RAISE only, so nothing stops it). featGrants.bonusSkillFeat exists but injects an UNRESTRICTED skill-feat slot; there is no way to say 'a skill feat for the skill you just picked'. Both need engine work. The trailing 'first time each day you succeed... +3 status bonus to your next check within the hour' has no lane at all and should stay prose.

name: Offensive Boost
restriction: Swappable with downtime, the same way modifications are switched.

engineNote: The MENU fits `effectChoices` on a classFeature (13 already do), but the EFFECT does not: EffectGrant has no 'extra damage dice on Strikes' field at all, so the pick can be stored and displayed but will not reach the strike-damage breakdown. The armor-innovation branch also carries a SECOND, daily choice — "one weapon you choose during daily preparations" — which is a per-day inventory-weapon pick with no lane (the record's own trailing note flags this: "the included effect is only needed for construct innovations and armor innovations for selecting their daily preparation weapon").

Stumbling — Stage 1: no adjustment; Stage 2: off-guard; Stage 3: off-guard and −5-foot penalty to Speed

name: Barbarian Dedication
chooses: other (barbarian instinct — a class subclass option)
restriction: You have the instinct "for all purposes" but gain none of its other abilities; you ARE bound by its anathema.
effect: Satisfies instinct prerequisites (so Basic Fury etc. can grant instinct-gated barbarian feats such as Animalistic Brutality), and applies the instinct's anathema. It must NOT grant the instinct's rage-damage tier.
evidence: "Choose an instinct as you would if you were a barbarian. You have that instinct for all purposes, but you don't gain any of the other abilities it grants."
engineNote: The SKILL half is already done (core.json ships effectChoices 'barbarian-dedication-skill' with 15 skill options). The INSTINCT half is unmodelled: src/rules/derive.ts reads RAGE_DAMAGE[c.subclassId] only when c.classId === 'barbarian', and the archetype branch is a hardcoded flat +2 — correct RAW, and the instinct pick must not change it. Needs an archetype-subclass lane; the precedent already exists (BuildState.archetypeEidolonType stores a summoner subclass option id for Summoner Dedication), so this would be the second such field. Use `choice`/featChoices for storage if the prerequisite validator can read it, otherwise a dedicated BuildState field.

name: Perfection's Path
restriction: Only a save you are already an EXPERT in.
effect: That saving throw's proficiency rank becomes master.
evidence: "Choose one saving throw (Fortitude, Reflex, or Will) in which you are an expert. Your proficiency rank in the chosen saving throw increases to master."
engineNote: FULLY EXPRESSIBLE TODAY — exactly the Canny Acumen pattern: a `choice` (kind 'array') plus FEAT_GRANTS.choiceGrants keyed by the same values, e.g. { fortitude: { save: { fortitude: 'master' } }, reflex: {...}, will: {...} }. choiceGrants keys must match the stored choice value verbatim. Minor caveat: FeatGrant.save RAISES only and there is no conditional-save lane (conditionalSkills exists but is skills-only), so picking a save you're merely trained in would jump you straight to master; the 'expert in at least one saving throw' prerequisite is stored as free text and isn't validated per option. Low-severity over-grant, worth a conditionalSaves lane later.

evidence: "Choose a Mystery. You become trained in Religion and the mystery's skill; if you were already trained, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the curse associated with your mystery"
engineNote: Currently only APPROXIMATED: src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts has 'oracle-dedication': { skills: { religion: 'trained' }, skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }], redundantFallback: true } — i.e. the mystery's own skill is collapsed into a generic any-skill pick, and the CURSE is not granted at all. The data needed is present: core.json classes.oracle subclass options carry grants.skills (e.g. ancestors → society) and a Curse of … in descRefs. Needs the same archetype-subclass lane as Barbarian Dedication (precedent: BuildState.archetypeEidolonType), which would then also feed Domain Acumen and Domain Fluency. The spellcasting half is already handled by CASTER_ARCHETYPES['oracle-dedication'].

name: Sorcerer Dedication
chooses: other (sorcerer bloodline — a class subclass option)
restriction: "You don't gain any other abilities from your choice of bloodline" — no blood magic, no bloodline focus spells from the dedication itself.
effect: Trained in the bloodline's TWO skills (each already-trained one converting to a free skill pick), and the bloodline's tradition becomes the archetype's spell tradition and constrains the two cantrips (its list, plus the bloodline's granted spells).

engineNote: Currently only APPROXIMATED in two places: (1) CASTER_ARCHETYPES marks it choiceTradition: true, so the builder asks the player to pick a TRADITION directly (BuildState.archetypeTradition) instead of deriving it from a bloodline; (2) featGrantsAuto has 'sorcerer-dedication': { skillChoices: [{ options:'any', rank:'trained' }, { options:'any', rank:'trained' }] } — two generic free skills instead of the bloodline's two specific skills with a redundancy fallback. The data is present: classes.sorcerer subclass options carry `tradition`, `grants.skills` (2 each) and `grantedSpells`. A real bloodline pick would set tradition + both skills automatically and give Crossblooded Evolution / Greater Crossblooded Evolution and Advanced/Greater Bloodline something to hang off. Same archetype-subclass lane as Barbarian and Oracle Dedication.

name: Bestiary Scholar
restriction: You must have master proficiency in the chosen skill — the feat's own prerequisite ('master in Arcana, Crafting, Nature, Occultism, or Religion') already gates this.
effect: Record + display only. The chosen skill may Recall Knowledge to identify any creature normally identified by any of the five. The '+1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll or saving throw' only fires after a critical identification, so it is an in-play conditional, not a standing modifier.
evidence: "When you gain this feat, choose one of the following skills in which you have attained master proficiency: Arcana, Crafting, Nature, Occultism, or Religion."
engineNote: Nothing new required: the pick round-trips through FeatChoice.choice and renders on the feat card. Note FeatChoiceDef has no proficiency filter, so all five options are always offered even to a character who is only expert — acceptable, since the prerequisite blocks the feat anyway.

name: Masterful Obfuscation
openSource: Any skill with the Recall Knowledge action in which you are master — Arcana, Crafting, Medicine, Nature, Occultism, Religion, Society, or any Lore skill you have.
restriction: master proficiency, and the skill must have a Recall Knowledge use. The feat's prerequisite ('master in a skill with the Recall Knowledge action') restates it.
effect: Display only. When you Lie about facts related to that subject you roll the CHOSEN skill in place of Deception, carrying that skill's bonuses/penalties. No standing modifier changes.

engineNote: FeatChoiceDef.kind is currently only 'domains' | 'array' — an open skill pool is a new kind. It must include free-text Lore (the text says 'one skill with the Recall Knowledge action', and Lore qualifies), which the existing BuildState.featLoreChoices free-text input already solves for FEAT_GRANTS.loreChoices; the same widget would need to be reachable from a choice. Fallback with zero engine work: kind 'array' over the seven non-Lore RK skills, which silently drops the Lore case.

restriction: Must be one of the three innate spells the Lore Seeker feat granted (prerequisite: Lore Seeker).

engineNote: The pick has to reach back and MUTATE ANOTHER feat's grant: lore-seeker.innateSpells currently reads [translate, sound-body, see-the-unseen] each usesPerDay:1, rank:2. InnateSpellGrant already has usesPerDay / rank / heightenHalfLevel, so every value is expressible — what is missing is a lane for one feat to override another feat's innate grant. DATA DEFECT: this record's description still uses the pre-Remaster names (comprehend language / restore senses / see invisibility) while lore-seeker in core.json already uses the Remaster names; the option values above are the Remaster ids that actually exist in d.spells.

name: Martial Exercise
restriction: None beyond the group list (the 17 weapon groups present in core.json items).
effect: A MIRRORING proficiency grant: whenever any weapon proficiency rank rises to expert or beyond, simple AND martial weapons of the chosen group also gain that rank.

engineNote: FEAT_GRANTS already has the exact semantics one level down: weaponFamiliarity.mirrorBestCategory ('whenever a class feature grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons, you also gain it for these') — but it is keyed to NAMED weapons. Proficiencies.weaponGroups exists but holds a flat rank, not a mirror. Needs a group-shaped sibling, e.g. weaponGroupFamiliarity: { group: <from choice.value>, categories: ['simple','martial'], mirrorBestCategory: true }, fed by the feat's choice value the way choiceGrants already works.

name: Kreighton's Cognitive Crossover
restriction: Two DIFFERENT skills from the list; the feat's whole function is reattempting with 'the other chosen skill'. No proficiency requirement. Picking 'Lore (any one)' needs a follow-up free-text subject.
effect: Display only — no proficiency or modifier changes. The pair defines the reaction's trigger (a fruitless Recall Knowledge with one of them) and its reroll skill (the other).

engineNote: Feat.choice is singular, so two picks do not fit it. name: Animal Shape
restriction: Locked once taken — the text forbids changing it later, so it is a genuinely permanent build value (unlike most 'choose a form' text).
